brief: Goldman's Pasquariello says the primary S&P/NDX uptrend remains intact, but with less conviction than at any point since summer, after the OpenAI-headline pullback from Tuesday's 7,818 high to 7,765. His six claims chain together: the trend is up because AI drives it; positioning sits at 1/3/5-year net-exposure lows except for Mag7 (about 22% of Prime Book US exposure, a record) and semis (12%, double January's level), so low net coexists with high gross risk concentrated in one trade; 28% Q3 S&P EPS growth (up from 27%) discourages shorting even as median-stock growth slows from 14% to 9%, the top 10 names will generate 68% of EPS growth (up from 48% last quarter) with Micron and Nvidia alone half of that, and both earnings growth and hyperscaler capex growth (above 100%) are at a cycle peak; rising rates (30Y auction at 5.618%, highest since 2000; 10Y at 5.23%) have shifted from a headwind to a bigger risk for sovereigns and corporates because AI capex is crowding out government funding. He concludes these are facets of one trade: the bull case needs AI earnings and capex to keep delivering while rates stay contained; the bear case needs only one leg to fail.
